official.deadline_note: BI publishes the scholarship deadline only as 'March 1' with no calendar year on the scholarship page; the central scholarships overview page lists 1 March as the deadline for all applicants to master programmes. Related published dates: the full-time application portal opens 1 November, applicants from outside the EU/EEA who need a residence permit must apply by 15 June, and the master application web closes 1 August. No dated deadline for the next intake is published yet.
official.application_cycle: Annual autumn intake. The currently published wording on the Bergen page is that only candidates admitted to a Master of Science programme at campus Bergen commencing Autumn 2026 will be considered for this scholarship; the portal for the next intake opens 1 November.
official.status_note: The scholarship page currently scopes the award to candidates admitted to an MSc programme at campus Bergen commencing Autumn 2026, whose 1 March scholarship deadline has passed. BI's next full-time intake cycle opens when the application portal opens on 1 November, with 1 March as the standing master scholarship deadline and decisions notified by the end of April.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: 'The scholarship will cover full tuition fees for up to two years if the student maintains the academic progression requirements for scholarship recipients.' BI's published 2026-27 standard master tuition fee is NOK 128 200 per academic year (EUR 10 994 / USD 12 663); full-time students with citizenship from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland pay a 30% differential, published as NOK 166 700 for 2026-27.

GMAT or GRE test score, forwarded directly from the test centre or uploaded as a copy of the score report

One-page CV covering relevant education, work experience, volunteering and academic or leadership engagements
Scholarship application letter of maximum one page, combined with the CV into a single PDF
Copy of the passport identification page and a financial declaration on BI's template

official.application_route: A single submission in BI's online application portal: apply for admission to an MSc programme at campus Bergen and upload the CV plus one-page scholarship letter as one PDF in the 'Scholarship' section of the same application.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to candidates with international citizenship who are not residents of Norway. International citizens who completed a bachelor's degree in Norway, or who are eligible for a Laanekassen tuition reduction/loan, are treated as domestic applicants and are not eligible.
official.international_eligibility: Yes, by design the award is for candidates with international citizenship who are not residents of Norway.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Must be admitted to a Master of Science degree programme at campus Bergen. BI lists Master in Business with a major in Finance and Master in Leadership and Organisational Psychology as the two master's degrees at campus Bergen. Awarded scholarships are tied to a specific academic programme at a designated campus and cannot be transferred.
official.duration: Up to two years of full tuition fees; BI master programmes last two academic years
official.description: BI presents this as an entrance scholarship 'awarded to applicants with a strong academic record admitted to any MSc programme at campus Bergen', which 'will cover full tuition fees for up to two years if the student maintains the academic progression requirements for scholarship recipients'. BI stresses that competition for scholarships is great, that awards are based on academic merit rather than financial need, and that recipients must be prepared to act as BI Ambassadors.
official.program_type: Merit-based entrance scholarship covering full tuition fees for Master of Science studies at campus Bergen
official.english_requirement: IELTS Academic overall 6.5, TOEFL iBT overall 90, Pearson PTE Academic 62, or University of Cambridge C1 Advanced (176) / C2 Proficiency (180); home editions are accepted (TOEFL iBT Special Home Edition 90, IELTS Indicator 6.5). Native English speakers and applicants who have completed two or more academic years of study taught in English may request a waiver. Applicants must have taken an English aptitude test, and GMAT/GRE, before 1 March to be considered for a scholarship, and conditional offers are not granted without them.

Award wording ('full tuition fees for up to two years'), the 1 March deadline, the GPA 4.0 ECTS threshold, the Bergen-campus MSc restriction, the academic progression rules and the English/GMAT admission thresholds were all confirmed on BI's own domain. applicant_utility.summary: This award pays your BI master's tuition at Bergen for up to two years, but it puts no money in your bank account: living costs, flights, housing and the student-welfare membership are all on you, and BI's own published living-expense estimate for 2026-27 is NOK 151 690 a year. The eligible programme pool is deliberately tiny, because BI runs only two master's degrees in Bergen, Master in Business with a major in Finance and Master in Leadership and Organisational Psychology, so the scholarship only exists if you are admitted to one of those. Selection is a pure grades contest with no needs test, and the gate that sinks most applicants is timing: no GMAT/GRE and English test in hand by 1 March means no scholarship consideration at all. It is also a renewal, not a grant: you keep it by banking 30 ECTS every semester and a cumulative B, so plan your course load around protecting the award.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-GPA international applicants, not resident in Norway, who want a two-year BI master's at Bergen in finance or leadership/organisational psychology and can self-fund roughly NOK 300 000 in living costs across the degree.
application_readiness_checklist: Book GMAT (Focus 555 / 10th edition 600) or GRE (158 Quantitative) and IELTS/TOEFL/PTE early enough to have verified scores in hand before 1 March; BI will not consider you for a scholarship without them
Confirm your status is genuinely international for scholarship purposes: no Norwegian bachelor's, no Laanekassen entitlement, and no Norwegian residency that reclassifies you as domestic
Draft the one-page scholarship letter around academic record and fit with the Bergen programme, then merge it with your one-page CV into a single PDF before uploading
Assemble the full admission file at the same time (transcripts with grade-scale explanation, test scores, passport, financial declaration) because nothing can be added after submission
Accept the BI admission offer promptly; the scholarship file is only reviewed after you accept, and unaccepted scholarship offers get reallocated to another candidate
Map out a 30 ECTS per semester study plan for both years and check the cumulative-B trajectory before you accept, since the award is withdrawn if progression slips
common_rejection_risks: No GMAT/GRE and English test result before 1 March, which BI states outright excludes you from scholarship consideration and blocks even a conditional offer
Missing the 1 March deadline, since late scholarship applications will not be considered even though admission itself rolls on to 1 August
Being silently reclassified as a domestic applicant because you hold a Norwegian bachelor's degree or qualify for a Laanekassen reduction or loan
Uploading the CV and letter as two separate files, or missing the 'Scholarship' tab in the portal, so the file is never assessed
Not accepting the admission offer, or accepting a scholarship offer after its stated expiry date, at which point it is withdrawn and given to someone else
Already holding a master's degree, or applying to an MSc that is not one of the two Bergen programmes, which voids eligibility for this specific award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living expenses, which BI estimates at NOK 151 690 per year for 2026-27, are entirely self-funded, as are flights, housing, course reading, course excursions, the per-semester student organisation membership and any re-sit examination fees (NOK 330 per credit). Students from outside the EU/EEA must also show a deposit covering tuition plus one year of living expenses for the residence permit, for each year of the programme.
document_audit: Transcripts and diplomas must be in English or a Scandinavian language, or certified translations accompanied by the originals, and must include an official explanation of the grading scale
Have IELTS/TOEFL/PTE results sent directly from the test centre where possible; IELTS copies are only accepted if the TRF number is visible, and BI's TOEFL code is 0529
GRE scores go under BI institution code 0497, while GMAT has no institution code: search for BI in the institution field
The CV and scholarship letter must be a single combined PDF, and the letter is capped at one page, so trim before you merge
The financial declaration must follow BI's own template and the passport copy must show the photo and legal name page
Documentation is frozen at submission: BI accepts no additional documents once the application is in
alerts: 1 March is the scholarship gate, not the admission gate: admission continues on a rolling basis to 1 August, but a scholarship application after 1 March is dead
Applicants from outside the EU/EEA must apply by 15 June to allow time for a student residence permit, which sits well after the scholarship deadline
Scholarship decisions arrive separately from the admission offer, most are awarded in late April, and all decisions are final and cannot be appealed
BI awards only one scholarship per applicant even if you apply for several, and the award is tied to one programme and campus and cannot be transferred
Recipients take on BI Ambassador duties, including recruitment support, and must sustain 30 ECTS per semester plus a cumulative B to keep the tuition coverage
The currently published cycle wording covers students commencing Autumn 2026, so watch the scholarship overview page from 1 November for the next cycle's confirmation
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One online application in BI's portal covering admission and the scholarship together, then accept the admission offer and wait for a separate scholarship decision communicated by the end of April.
